intro.en: Suicide is built from two Latin pieces meaning of oneself and to kill.
intro.cn: suicide 由两个拉丁语成分构成，分别表示「自己」和「杀」。

items.en: Sui meant of oneself.
items.cn: sui 意为「自己的」。

items.en: Caedere meant to kill or cut down.
items.cn: caedere 意为杀死或砍倒。

items.en: Suicidium named the killing of oneself.
items.cn: suicidium 指杀死自己的行为。

items.en: Suicide entered English with that sense.
items.cn: suicide 以这个含义进入英语。

items.en: It later extended to suicide attacks.
items.cn: 后来它又扩展到自杀式袭击。

note.en: Suicide is compared with other -cide words and with words for self-harm.
note.cn: 把 suicide 与其他以 -cide 结尾的词以及表示自伤的词作比较。

definition_en: a meeting of many people, the fitting together of parts, or a law-making body
core_image: 大厅里人群坐满，或零件排成一列装上
scene: 周一早晨全校都到操场上站好。 The whole school attends assembly on Monday.

definition_en: the bags, cases and other containers that a traveller carries, spoken of as a group without a plural, or in older use the baggage that moved with an army
core_image: 几只贴满标签的箱子堆在门口，拉杆还没收起
scene: 出发前一晚，客厅地板上堆着几只箱子和旅行袋，拉链还敞着。 She packed her luggage the night before the flight and left it by the door.
sceneCN: 这里 luggage 是「行李、旅行箱包的总称」（第 1 个义项：旅行者随身携带的箱包）；句意为她出发前一晚收拾好行李，把它放在门边。图中可辨识物件：客厅地板、行李箱、旅行袋。

senses.title: Bags and cases carried on a journey
senses.definition: the bags, suitcases and other containers in which a traveller carries personal things
senses.definitionCN: 旅行者用来装个人物品的箱包等容器的总称
senses.example: She packed her luggage the night before the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前一晚，她收拾好了行李。
senses.why: The word began as the mass of things lugged along on a journey, so it names the load as a whole rather than each separate bag; English keeps it uncountable because the group, not the item, is what the word points at.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指旅途中被拖着走的那一堆东西，命名的是整批负担而不是某一只包；英语让它保持不可数，因为词所指向的是这一整堆，而不是其中的单件。

senses.title: An item counted by the piece
senses.definition: a traveller's bags when they are counted or weighed one piece at a time, as at an airport desk
senses.definitionCN: 在机场柜台等场合按件数或重量逐件清点的旅行箱包
senses.example: How many pieces of luggage are you checking in?
senses.exampleCN: 你要托运几件行李？
senses.why: Because the noun has no plural of its own, English counts the load through a phrase such as a piece of; the piece becomes the unit while the word itself stays collective.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词本身没有复数形式，英语便借「一件」这样的说法来计数；于是「件」成了单位，而这个词本身仍保持集体含义。

senses.title: The baggage of an army
senses.definition: in older use, the carts, supplies and bags that moved with an army on the march
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指随军队行进的车马、补给与包袋
senses.example: The column halted while its luggage was brought up.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍停下来，等辎重跟上来。
senses.why: An army on the march drags the same kind of load as a traveller, so the word was widened from personal bags to the whole train of supplies that follows the soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 行军中的军队拖着与旅人同类的一堆东西，于是这个词从个人箱包扩展到跟随士兵的整套补给车队。

intro.en: Luggage is an English noun usually explained as the verb lug plus the suffix -age, and it has meant both a traveller's bags and an army's baggage.
intro.cn: luggage 是一个英语名词，一般解释为动词 lug 加后缀 -age 构成；它既指旅行者的箱包，也指军队的辎重。

items.en: The earliest luggage names the mass of bags and gear dragged along on a journey, and the same word could also mean a bundle tied up for carrying.
items.cn: 最早的 luggage 指旅途中被拖着走的那一堆包袋与器具，同一个词也可指捆好待扛的一束东西。

items.en: It is generally explained as the verb lug, to drag or carry with effort, plus the noun suffix -age; the deeper origin of lug itself is uncertain, so the chain is plausible rather than proved.
items.cn: 一般认为它由动词 lug（吃力地拖、扛）加名词后缀 -age 构成；但 lug 本身更早的来源并不确定，所以这条构词链只能算合理推断，而非定论。

items.en: By the sixteenth century luggage settles on the bags of a traveller, while the older military sense survives for the baggage train of an army.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，luggage 稳定指旅行者的箱包，而更早的军事义仍保留下来，用来指军队的辎重队。

items.en: Steamers and railways made luggage a fixed term for personal bags, and British usage kept it while American usage preferred baggage.
items.cn: 轮船与铁路使 luggage 成为指个人行李的固定说法，英式沿用这个词，美式则更常用 baggage。

items.en: Modern English keeps luggage uncountable, counts it in pieces, and builds compounds such as hand luggage and luggage allowance.
items.cn: 现代英语让 luggage 保持不可数，用「件」来计数，并构成 hand luggage、luggage allowance 之类的复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the root verb and the compounds built on luggage; the near-meaning group gathers other words for bags and travel loads.
note.cn: 形近组收它的词根动词以及由 luggage 构成的复合词；近义组收其他表示箱包与旅途负载的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a verb for dragging, and its family keeps returning to loads that are hauled rather than neatly carried.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「拖拽」的动词上，同族词反复回到被拖着走、而非轻巧提着的负载。

normal.en: Luggage rests on the verb lug, to drag something heavy, so the word pictures bags being hauled along a platform.
normal.cn: luggage 建立在动词 lug（吃力地拖）之上，所以这个词画出的画面是在站台上拖着一堆包走。

normal.en: The suffix -age turns a verb into a mass noun, which is why luggage has no plural and behaves like baggage.
normal.cn: 后缀 -age 把动词变成集体名词，所以 luggage 没有复数，用法与 baggage 相同。

normal.en: British travellers say luggage where Americans often say baggage, and neither word takes an s.
normal.cn: 英国旅客说 luggage，美国人常说 baggage，两个词都不加 s。

normal.en: Hand luggage stays with the passenger while check-in luggage goes into the hold, so the compounds sort the load by where it travels.
normal.cn: hand luggage 随乘客走，check-in luggage 进舱底，这些复合词按行李的去处分门别类。

normal.en: A luggage tag carries your name because a bag pulled off a belt belongs to nobody until it is marked.
normal.cn: 行李牌上写着名字，因为从传送带上取下的包在没有标记之前不属于任何人。

abstract.en: A word for dragged bags suggests that travel is measured less by distance than by what you insist on carrying.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拖行李」的词暗示，衡量旅程的不是距离，而是你坚持要带走的东西。

abstract.en: Luggage has no plural because a traveller's load is felt as one weight rather than as separate objects.
abstract.cn: luggage 没有复数，因为旅人的负载被感受为一整个重量，而不是分开的物件。

abstract.en: Every bag has a tag, and every tag is a small claim that says this weight is mine.
abstract.cn: 每只包都有牌子，每块牌子都是一个微小的声明：这份重量属于我。

items.exampleCN: 这张票包含相当宽松的行李额度。

definition_zh: 报摊；书报亭；报刊零售处；报摊零售价
definition_en: a small open booth or metal frame on a pavement where newspapers and magazines are sold
core_image: 街角铁架上整排报纸夹在木夹子里，最上面一份还翻开着
scene: 天刚亮，街角的铁架上已经夹好一排报纸，摊主把硬币盒摆到前排。 The newsstand opens before the first bus passes.
sceneCN: 这里 newsstand 是「街头报摊」（第 1 个义项：在街边卖报纸杂志的摊位）；句意为报摊在第一班公交车经过之前就开了门。图中可辨识物件：铁架、木夹子、硬币盒。

pos.zh: 报摊；书报亭；报刊零售处

derivatives.zh: newsstand 的前一个构件，源自古英语 neowe（新的）的复数 neowes，义为「新闻；消息」
newsstand 的后一个构件，源自古英语 stondan（站立），义为「摊位；架子」
由 news 与 paper 复合而成，义为「报纸」
由 news 与 agent（经营者）复合而成，义为「报刊经销商；报刊店」

senses.title: A street stand that sells papers
senses.definition: a small open booth or metal frame on a pavement where newspapers and magazines are sold
senses.definitionCN: 人行道上出售报纸和杂志的小型敞开摊位或金属架
senses.example: He bought a paper at the newsstand near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站附近的报摊买了一份报纸。
senses.why: The compound puts the goods in front of the place: news names the printed reports, and stand names the frame that holds them at eye level, so the word marks a spot defined by what it displays.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把货物摆在地点前面：news 指印出来的新闻，stand 指把报纸架到视线高度的架子，所以这个词标记的是一个由「摆什么」来定义的位置。

senses.title: The price of a copy bought on the street
senses.definition: the full price charged for a single copy at a stand, as opposed to the lower rate offered to subscribers
senses.definitionCN: 在摊上买一份所付的全价，与提供给订户的较低价格相对
senses.example: The magazine costs less by subscription than at newsstand price.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志订阅价比报摊零售价低。
senses.why: Once a stand counts as a recognised place of sale, its price turns into a measuring stick, so publishers quote the newsstand price to set the ordinary buyer's cost against the subscriber's saving.
senses.whyCN: 报摊一旦算作公认的售卖点，它的价格就变成一把尺子，因此出版方用「报摊价」把普通买者付的钱与订户省下的钱放在一起对照。

senses.title: A single copy sold from a stand
senses.definition: one physical copy of a publication bought from a stand rather than received through delivery
senses.definitionCN: 从摊上买到、而不是通过投递收到的那一份实物刊物
senses.example: Collectors hunt for the newsstand copy with the early cover.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏者专门找那种封面是早期版本的报摊零售本。
senses.why: Because the stand sells units one at a time, the word slips from the place to the object handed across the counter, marking the copy that never travelled by post.
senses.whyCN: 因为报摊是一份一份地卖，这个词就从地点滑到柜台递出的东西，专指那本没有走过邮路的本子。

senses.title: The trade of keeping a stand open
senses.definition: the daily business of ordering stock, opening early and selling papers from a fixed pitch
senses.definitionCN: 每天进货、早早开张、在固定点位卖报的营生
senses.example: Running a newsstand means being at the corner before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 经营报摊意味着天没亮就得守在街角。
senses.why: A stand is also a way of earning a living, so the same noun covers the furniture and the livelihood standing behind it, since a fixed pitch and a daily routine belong to both.
senses.whyCN: 报摊同时也是一种谋生方式，所以同一个名词既指那件家什，也指撑在它背后的生计，因为固定的点位与每天的作息同属两者。

intro.en: Newsstand is a plain English compound of two common words, and its history is mostly the history of its two halves rather than of a borrowed root.
intro.cn: newsstand 是两个普通英语词拼成的复合词，它的来历主要是两个构件各自的来历，而不是某个借来的词根。

items.en: The first element goes back to a reconstructed root for new, the same source that produced Latin novus and Greek neos.
items.cn: 第一个构件可上溯到一个表示「新」的重构词根，拉丁语 novus 与希腊语 neos 都出自这里。

items.en: Neowe meant new, and its plural neowes, literally new things, became the noun news in Middle English.
items.cn: neowe 意为新的，它的复数 neowes 字面是「一件件新事」，到中古英语变成名词 news。

items.en: Stondan meant to stand, and from it came the noun stand for the place where a person or a thing stands and stays.
items.cn: stondan 意为站立，由它产生名词 stand，指人或物站定、停留的位置。

items.en: The two words were joined for the frame at a street corner that holds papers, a use that dictionaries generally date to the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 两个词被合起来指街角夹放报纸的架子，一般认为这种用法可追到十八世纪。

items.en: Modern English applies the word to the booth, the price printed on a cover and the single copy sold there, and it stays on even where a machine replaces the stand.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词用于摊位本身、封面上印的零售价，以及在那里卖出的单份刊物；即使机器取代了摊位，这些说法仍然留着。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the two halves of the compound and the people who work with papers; the near-meaning group collects other places built for selling printed goods.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两个构件以及与报纸打交道的词；近义组收其他为售卖印刷品而设的场所。

entries.definition: A printed sheet of news sold daily or weekly.
entries.definitionCN: 每天或每周出售的印有新闻的纸张；报纸。

entries.definition: A shopkeeper who sells newspapers and magazines, chiefly in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 主要在英国英语中使用的说法，指售卖报纸杂志的店主。

entries.definition: A boy who used to deliver or call out papers on the street.
entries.definitionCN: 旧时在街上送报或叫卖报纸的男孩。

entries.definition: A frame or small structure set up for display or sale.
entries.definitionCN: 为陈列或售卖而搭起的架子或小结构。

entries.definition: A small booth in a public place selling papers, drinks or tickets.
entries.definitionCN: 公共场所售卖报纸、饮料或票券的小亭。

entries.definition: A stall or open stand where books, papers and magazines are sold.
entries.definitionCN: 售卖书籍、报纸和杂志的摊位或敞开货架。

entries.definition: A person who sells goods from a stand or in the street.
entries.definitionCN: 在摊位或街头售卖货物的人。

entries.definition: A small enclosed or open structure used for selling or for a service.
entries.definitionCN: 用于售卖或提供服务的封闭或敞开的小结构。

normalIntro.en: The compound is transparent, news on a stand; what is worth remembering is how each half grew and how the price and the copy took the name of the place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词是透明的：架子上的新闻。值得记住的是两个构件各自怎么长成，以及价格和单份刊物如何借用了这个地点的名字。

normal.en: News began as the plural of new, so it once meant new things rather than a mass of reports.
normal.cn: news 起初是 new 的复数，本来指一件件新事，而不是一堆报道。

normal.en: Stand is the noun from the verb to stand, so a newsstand is the frame that stands and waits for buyers.
normal.cn: stand 是从动词「站立」来的名词，所以报摊就是站在那儿等买主的架子。

normal.en: English often names a shop by what it displays rather than by who owns it, which is why this word begins with news.
normal.cn: 英语常按陈列的东西而不是按主人来给店铺命名，所以这个词以 news 开头。

normal.en: The price printed on a cover is called the newsstand price because that is where the full rate is charged.
normal.cn: 封面上印的价格叫「报摊价」，就是因为在那里收的是全价。

normal.en: A newsstand copy is the opposite of a delivered copy, so the word can jump from the furniture to the paper in your hand.
normal.cn: 报摊零售本与投递到家的本子相对，所以这个词能从架子跳到手里的报纸。

abstract.en: A stand is furniture, a price and a trade at once, because one fixed spot can support all three.
abstract.cn: 报摊同时是家具、价格和营生，因为同一个固定点位能撑起这三样东西。

abstract.en: The word puts the goods before the place, a quiet admission that a stall exists only for what it can show.
abstract.cn: 这个词把货物放在地点之前，等于坦白：摊位只为它能摆出来的东西而存在。

abstract.en: When a machine replaces the stand, the old word survives on the price and the copy, which is how places outlive their furniture.
abstract.cn: 当机器取代了摊位，旧词仍留在价格和单份刊物上，地点就是这样比它的家什活得更久。

examples.en: He bought a paper at the newsstand near the station.
examples.cn: 他在车站附近的报摊买了一份报纸。

examples.en: The newsstand price is higher than the yearly subscription.
examples.cn: 报摊零售价高于全年订阅价。

examples.en: She runs a newsstand on the corner and knows every regular customer.
examples.cn: 她在街角经营一个报摊，认得每一位老主顾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛事摊」——摊上每天都有一堆牛大的事等着登报；记住 newsstand 是报摊。

root: news（新闻，源自古英语 neowe「新的」的复数 neowes）加 stand（源自古英语 stondan「站立」）复合而成，指街角夹放报刊的架子，一般认为十八世纪起用。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the frame that holds papers at a corner; the senses split into its price, its single copies and the trade of keeping it open.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是街角夹放报刊的架子；义项由此分成它标示的价格、它卖出的单份刊物，以及把它撑起来的营生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of papers pegged on a metal frame at a street corner, one copy still open.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角铁架上一排用夹子夹住的报纸，其中一份还翻开着。

branches.en: a metal frame pegged with papers before sunrise
branches.cn: 日出前夹满报纸的铁架

branches.en: a hand taking coins over a narrow counter
branches.cn: 在窄柜台前递过硬币的手

branches.en: a cover price printed beside the barcode
branches.cn: 印在条形码旁的封面价

branches.en: a folded copy that never went by post
branches.cn: 一份没走过邮路的折起报纸

branches.en: a shutter lifted at the corner before the first bus
branches.cn: 第一班公交车之前拉起的街角卷帘

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English words for new things and for standing, and each half brings its own family along.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语中表示「新事」和「站立」的两个词构成，两个构件各自带来自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: The compound is English and its first element is native; it is linked to Latin novus only through a reconstructed root, so no reliable Latin source word is recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词属于英语，第一个构件是本族词；它只通过一个重构词根与拉丁语 novus 有远亲关系，因此这里不记可靠的拉丁语源词。

definition_en: to change and improve something written, or to study again
core_image: 一页写满批注的稿纸，边角已经卷起
scene: 编辑在页边写下新的批注，要求作者修改第三章。 The editor wrote fresh comments in the margin and asked the author to revise the third chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 revise 是「修改、修订」（第 1 个义项：改动文字使其更好）；句意：编辑在页边写下新的批注，要求作者修改第三章。

senses.title: Improving a text
senses.definition: to change a piece of writing to improve it
senses.definitionCN: 改动文字使其更好
senses.example: He revised the report three times.
senses.exampleCN: 他把报告修改了三遍。
senses.why: Re- plus visere, to look at, gives the sense of looking again to improve.
senses.whyCN: re- 加 visere（看）表示再看一遍以求改进。

senses.title: Studying for a test
senses.definition: to study lessons again before an exam
senses.definitionCN: 考试前再次学习功课
senses.example: British students revise for exams in May.
senses.exampleCN: 英国学生在五月为考试复习。
senses.why: British English extends looking again to studying again.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把再看一遍延伸为再学一遍。

senses.title: Changing a plan
senses.definition: to change a plan or opinion after thinking again
senses.definitionCN: 重新考虑后改变计划或看法
senses.example: We revised our travel plans after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后我们调整了旅行计划。
senses.why: Any plan can be looked at again and improved.
senses.whyCN: 任何计划都能被重新审视并改进。

intro.en: Revise comes from Latin revisere, to look at again.
intro.cn: revise 源自拉丁语 revisere（再看）。

items.en: Revisere means to look at again.
items.cn: revisere 意为再看。

items.en: It joins re-, again, to visere, to view.
items.cn: 它由 re-（再）与 visere（看）组成。

items.en: French reviser carries the sense of looking over a text.
items.cn: 法语 reviser 带有通读文本的含义。

items.en: Revise first means to look at writing again.
items.cn: revise 最初指再次审视文字。

items.en: British English adds the sense of studying for exams.
items.cn: 英式英语增加了为考试复习的含义。

note.en: Revise changes a text, while review only looks at it again.
note.cn: revise 是改动文字，review 只是再看一遍。

entries.definition: the act of revising
a person who revises
changed and improved
to prepare text for publication
to make small changes to something
to make something right

normalIntro.en: Revise is to look again and make the text better.
normalIntro.cn: revise 是再看一遍并让文字更好。

normal.en: Revise a draft means improve the writing.
normal.cn: revise a draft 意为改进文字。

normal.en: Revise for an exam means study again.
normal.cn: revise for an exam 意为再次学习。

normal.en: A revised edition has been changed.
normal.cn: a revised edition 是经过修改的版本。

normal.en: Revise a plan means adjust it.
normal.cn: revise a plan 意为调整计划。

normal.en: Compare edit: edit can cut, revise usually improves.
normal.cn: 对比 edit：edit 可以删减，revise 通常是改进。

abstract.en: Picture a page with arrows and new sentences in the margin.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，页边画着箭头和新句子。

abstract.en: Imagine polishing a rough stone until it shines.
abstract.cn: 想象把粗糙的石头打磨到发亮。

abstract.en: Think of a second draft that is clearer than the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一份比初稿更清楚的二稿。

examples.en: The author revised the last chapter.
examples.cn: 作者修改了最后一章。

examples.en: She is revising for her history exam.
examples.cn: 她正在为历史考试复习。

examples.en: The company revised its budget.
examples.cn: 公司调整了预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ vise（看）」——再看一遍并动手改，就是修订、修改。

root: 拉丁语 revisere（再看）＝ re-（再）＋ visere（看）→ 法语 reviser → revise，核心义「再看一遍并加以改进」。

sensesIntro.en: Revise begins with improving a text, extends to British exam study, and finally to adjusting plans.
sensesIntro.cn: revise 从改进文字开始，延伸到英式英语的考试复习，最后指调整计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked-up manuscript with curled corners.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满批注、边角卷起的稿纸。

branches.en: Improving a text is the core use.
branches.cn: 改进文字是核心用法。

branches.en: British students look at lessons again.
branches.cn: 英国学生再学一遍功课。

branches.en: Plans are also looked at and changed.
branches.cn: 计划也会被重新审视和改动。

branches.en: Both writing and studying involve a second pass.
branches.cn: 写文章与学习都包含第二遍过程。

branches.en: Texts and plans can both be improved.
branches.cn: 文字与计划都能被改进。

intro.en: Revise joins re-, again, to the Latin root vis, to see.
intro.cn: revise 由 re-（再）与拉丁词根 vis（看）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and its form visere give the word its seeing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 及其变体 visere 提供了「看」的词根。

latinEntries.example: Visere is a frequentative form of videre.
latinEntries.exampleCN: visere 是 videre 的反复形式。

definition_zh: 运动的；运动员的；体格健壮的；擅长体育的
definition_en: physically strong, fit and good at sports, or relating to sports and exercise
core_image: 一个肌肉线条分明的人在跑道上轻快地跨过栏架
scene: 体育课上老师夸奖道： You have become strong and athletic after two years of training, always first in every race.
sceneCN: 这里指「体格健壮、擅长运动」（第 2 个义项：形容人身体强健、擅长体育）；句意为经过两年训练，你变得如此健壮敏捷。

pos.zh: 运动的；体育的；体格健壮的；擅长运动的

senses.title: Relating to sports and exercise
senses.definition: connected with sports, games and physical exercise
senses.definitionCN: 与体育、竞赛和身体锻炼有关的
senses.example: The school built a new athletic field last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 学校去年夏天建了新的运动场。
senses.why: Athletic first attaches itself to things: fields, shoes, programs — anything that belongs to the world of sport.
senses.whyCN: athletic 最早附着在事物上：运动场、运动鞋、体育项目——一切属于体育世界的东西。

senses.title: Physically strong and fit
senses.definition: having a strong, healthy body and moving well, like a trained sports person
senses.definitionCN: 身体强壮健康、动作协调，像受过训练的运动员那样
senses.example: Years of swimming kept her tall and athletic.
senses.exampleCN: 多年游泳让她身材高挑、体格健壮。
senses.why: When applied to a person, athletic paints the body an athlete would have: strong, lean, quick.
senses.whyCN: 当 athletic 用在人身上时，描绘的是运动员才有的身体：强壮、精瘦、敏捷。

senses.title: Good at sports
senses.definition: skillful at running, jumping and playing sports
senses.definitionCN: 擅长跑、跳及各类体育运动
senses.example: He is athletic and can play almost any ball game well.
senses.exampleCN: 他运动天赋好，几乎什么球类都打得好。
senses.why: Beyond the body, athletic also credits the ability: someone who wins at sports is called athletic.
senses.whyCN: 除了身体本身，athletic 也称赞能力：在运动中胜出的人常被称为 athletic。

senses.title: Active and energetic in style
senses.definition: describing clothes or designs made for movement and comfort
senses.definitionCN: 形容为方便活动、舒适而设计的服装或风格
senses.example: Athletic wear is now common on city streets, not only in gyms.
senses.exampleCN: 运动风服装如今常见于街头，不再只出现在健身房。
senses.why: Fashion borrowed the word for anything that suggests motion, sweat and freedom of movement.
senses.whyCN: 时尚界借用了这个词，形容一切暗示运动、流汗与活动自由的设计。

intro.en: athletic comes from Greek athletes (contestant) via athlete, with the English adjective suffix -ic.
intro.cn: athletic 来自希腊语 athletes（竞技者），经由 athlete 加英语形容词后缀 -ic 构成。

items.en: Greek athlon meant 'contest, prize'; athletes meant someone who competed for a prize.
items.cn: 希腊语 athlon 意为「竞赛、奖赏」；athletes 指为奖赏而竞赛的人。

items.en: Latin borrowed athleta for the competitor in public games.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 athleta，指公开竞技中的选手。

items.en: French athlétique carried the adjective sense into European learned vocabulary.
items.cn: 法语 athlétique 把形容词义带进欧洲学术词汇。

items.en: English athletic appears in the 1650s, first describing the games and exercises of ancient athletes.
items.cn: 英语 athletic 出现于 1650 年代，最初形容古代竞技者的比赛与操练。

items.en: From the 19th century athletic expanded to modern sports culture, sportswear and body type.
items.cn: 19 世纪起 athletic 扩展到现代体育文化、运动服装与体格描述。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root athl- family; group two holds near-meaning fitness adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 athl- 词根的词族；第二组是语义相近的体格类形容词。

entries.definition: The person who does sports; athletic is the adjective for that person or that world.
entries.definitionCN: 做运动的人；athletic 是形容该人或该领域的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for track and field sports; athletic describes, athletics names.
entries.definitionCN: 田径运动的名词；athletic 作描述，athletics 作名称。

entries.definition: The adverb: moves athletically means moves like a trained sports person.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式：动得 athletically 指动作像运动员一样。

entries.definition: Informal word for someone who likes or is good at sports; lighter than athletic.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中形容爱运动或擅长运动的人；比 athletic 更随意。

entries.definition: Describes big muscles only, without the skill side that athletic includes.
entries.definitionCN: 只形容肌肉发达，不含 athletic 所带的运动能力。

entries.definition: Healthy and in shape; broader than athletic, which also implies sports skill.
entries.definitionCN: 健康有型；范围比 athletic 广，但不强调运动技能。

normalIntro.en: athletic is simply athlete + -ic: everything that belongs to the athlete.
normalIntro.cn: athletic 就是 athlete + -ic：一切属于运动员的东西。

normal.en: athlete is inside the word: an athletic body looks like an athlete's body.
normal.cn: athlete 藏在词里：athletic 的身材就像运动员的身材。

normal.en: -ic turns nouns into adjectives, as in hero → heroic.
normal.cn: -ic 把名词变成形容词，如 hero → heroic。

normal.en: athletics (track and field) is the noun family member.
normal.cn: athletics（田径）是这个词族的名词成员。

normal.en: Greek athlon means prize: athletes once competed for prizes.
normal.cn: 希腊语 athlon 意为奖赏：athletes 原本就是为奖赏而赛的人。

normal.en: athletic shoes are shoes made for athletes.
normal.cn: athletic shoes 就是为运动员设计的鞋。

abstract.en: A chalk-dusted hand gripping a pull-up bar at dawn.
abstract.cn: 清晨，一只沾满镁粉的手握住单杠。

abstract.en: The lean silhouette of a runner against rising sun.
abstract.cn: 朝阳下奔跑者精瘦的剪影。

abstract.en: The springy feeling in legs after months of training.
abstract.cn: 数月训练后双腿弹性的感觉。

examples.en: Regular training made the whole rowing team strong and athletic.
examples.cn: 常年训练让整支赛艇队强壮而有运动能力。

examples.en: She wore her athletic gear even on rest days.
examples.cn: 她休息日也穿着运动装。

examples.en: The college offers athletic scholarships to talented runners.
examples.cn: 这所大学为有天赋的跑步选手提供体育奖学金。

dict_mnemonic.text: athlete（运动员）+ -ic（形容词后缀）= 运动员的；健壮的

root: 希腊语 athlon（竞赛、奖赏）→ athletes（竞技者）→ athlete → + -ic → athletic。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses spread from the athlete's world: things connected to sport, the strong body, the sports skill, and an energetic design style.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项围绕运动员的世界展开：与体育相关的事物、强健的体格、运动能力，以及充满力量感的设计风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lean runner clearing a hurdle in one smooth stride.
core.cn: 核心意象：精瘦的跑者一步流畅地跨过栏架。

branches.en: THINGS OF SPORT: fields, shoes, programs tied to exercise.
branches.cn: 体育之物：运动场、运动鞋、体育项目等与锻炼相关的事物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a strong body and the ability to play sports well.
branches.cn: 人本身：强健的身体和良好的运动能力。

branches.en: DESIGN: clothing and styles built for movement.
branches.cn: 设计：为活动而生的服装与风格。

branches.en: BODY TYPE: the athlete-like figure people train for.
branches.cn: 体格：人们锻炼所追求的运动员式身材。

branches.en: ENERGY: speed, power and freedom of movement in life and fashion.
branches.cn: 活力：生活与时尚中的速度、力量与活动自由。

intro.en: athletic is athlete + -ic; the Greek root athl- (contest) also gives athlete, athletics and biathlon.
intro.cn: athletic 由 athlete 加 -ic 构成；希腊词根 athl-（竞赛）还派生出 athlete、athletics、biathlon。

latinIntro.en: The root athl- is Greek, borrowed into Latin as athleta, then into European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 athl- 来自希腊语，拉丁语借为 athleta，之后进入欧洲各语言。

definition_zh: 条纹；斑纹；（军服上的）条纹
definition_en: a long narrow band of colour, a band on a uniform, or a kind or type of person
core_image: 斑马身上黑白相间的一道道长纹
scene: 斑马的条纹黑白相间。 A zebra's stripes are black and white.
sceneCN: 这里 stripe 是「条纹」（第 1 个义项）；句意：斑马的条纹黑白相间。

senses.title: A band of colour
senses.definition: a long narrow band of colour different from what is around it
senses.definitionCN: 与周围颜色不同的一条窄带
senses.example: A zebra's stripes are black and white.
senses.exampleCN: 斑马的条纹黑白相间。
senses.why: This is the pattern you see.
senses.whyCN: 这是眼睛看到的图案。

senses.title: A mark of rank
senses.definition: a band worn on a uniform to show rank
senses.definitionCN: 制服上表示军衔的条纹
senses.example: The sergeant has three stripes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位中士有三道军衔条。
senses.why: A band of cloth becomes a mark of standing.
senses.whyCN: 一条布带成了身份的标记。

senses.title: A type of person
senses.definition: a kind or group, as in people of all stripes
senses.definitionCN: 某种类型或群体，如各种类型的人
senses.example: The club welcomes people of all stripes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部欢迎各种各样的人。
senses.why: Different stripes mark different kinds.
senses.whyCN: 不同的条纹，标出不同的类别。

intro.en: Stripe comes from Middle English stripe, a band of colour.
intro.cn: stripe 来自中古英语 stripe，指一条色带。

items.en: Stripe named a narrow band.
items.cn: stripe 指一条窄带。

items.en: Related words named a line or stroke.
items.cn: 同源词表示线条或划痕。

items.en: Stripe described patterns on cloth and animals.
items.cn: stripe 描写布料与动物身上的花纹。

items.en: A uniform stripe marked rank.
items.cn: 制服上的条纹用来标示军衔。

items.en: Of all stripes came to mean of all kinds.
items.cn: of all stripes 引申为各种类型。

note.en: Stripe is compared with look-alike words and with words for lines and bands.
note.cn: 把 stripe 与形近词以及表示线条与色带的词作比较。

entries.definition: to remove a covering
to hit
ready to eat
a flat strip of material
a long thin mark
a long thin mark of colour

normalIntro.en: Stripe is a line of colour, a line of rank, or a line between kinds.
normalIntro.cn: stripe 是一道颜色的线、一道身份的线，或区分类型的线。

normal.en: The shirt has blue stripes.
normal.cn: 这件衬衫有蓝色条纹。

normal.en: Tigers have dark stripes.
normal.cn: 老虎身上有深色条纹。

normal.en: He earned his stripes in the army.
normal.cn: 他在军队里凭本事获得了认可。

normal.en: Writers of all stripes attended.
normal.cn: 各种各样的作家都出席了。

normal.en: A white stripe runs down the road.
normal.cn: 路面中间有一条白线。

abstract.en: A stripe is a line that repeats.
abstract.cn: 条纹，是一条不断重复的线。

abstract.en: Every uniform tells its rank in lines.
abstract.cn: 每套制服都用线条说明身份。

abstract.en: Different stripes, same cloth.
abstract.cn: 条纹不同，布是一样的。

examples.en: A zebra's stripes are black and white.
examples.cn: 斑马的条纹黑白相间。

examples.en: The sergeant has three stripes.
examples.cn: 这位中士有三道军衔条。

examples.en: The club welcomes people of all stripes.
examples.cn: 这个俱乐部欢迎各种各样的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: stripe 是一条窄色带；动物和衣服上的是条纹，制服上的是军衔条，不同条纹也代指不同类型的人。

root: 来自中古英语 stripe（色带），与表示线条、划痕的日耳曼语词相关；由视觉上的条纹，引申为制服上的军衔标记，再比喻人的类型与派别。

sensesIntro.en: Stripe is a band of colour, a mark of rank, or a label for a kind of person.
sensesIntro.cn: stripe 是一条色带、一个身份标记，或某一类人的标签。

core.en: Dark lines running down a pale coat.
core.cn: 深色线条沿着浅色皮毛延伸。

branches.en: A zebra crosses the road.
branches.cn: 一只斑马穿过道路。

branches.en: A sleeve carries three bands.
branches.cn: 袖子上有三道条。

branches.en: A crowd gathers from many groups.
branches.cn: 人群来自许多不同的群体。

branches.en: A pattern on cloth can carry meaning.
branches.cn: 布上的图案也能承载意义。

branches.en: Stripes mark both rank and kind.
branches.cn: 条纹既标身份，也标类别。

intro.en: Stripe forms a plural and two adjectives.
intro.cn: stripe 有复数形式，并能构成两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，源自日耳曼语。

items.example: A stripe of light crossed the floor.

items.exampleCN: 她很快凭本事获得了认可。

items.example: Readers of all stripes enjoy it.
items.exampleCN: 各种各样的读者都喜欢。

definition_en: costing a lot of money, or causing serious loss or damage
core_image: 一只钱包被打开，里面只剩几枚硬币和一张长账单
scene: 球队赢了决赛，却伤了两名主力，教练说这场胜利太贵了。 Winning the cup proved costly for the small club.
sceneCN: 这里 costly 指「代价惨重的」（第 2 个义项：带来严重损失）；句意是赢得奖杯对这家小俱乐部来说代价惨重。

senses.title: Very expensive
senses.definition: costing a great deal of money
senses.definitionCN: 需要花费大量金钱的
senses.example: The repairs were costly but necessary.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修很贵，却非做不可。
senses.why: A high price tag makes the hand stop before the pocket.
senses.whyCN: 高价签让手在伸向口袋之前停住。

senses.title: Paid for in loss
senses.definition: causing serious loss, damage or suffering
senses.definitionCN: 造成严重损失、损害或痛苦的
senses.example: Winning the cup proved costly for the small club.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得奖杯对这家小俱乐部来说代价惨重。
senses.why: Some bills arrive without money and are still paid in full.
senses.whyCN: 有些账单不用钱，却仍要全额偿付。

intro.en: Costly is cost plus the old adjective ending -ly, from Latin constare, to stand at a price.
intro.cn: costly 由 cost 加古形容词词尾 -ly 构成，根源是拉丁语 constare（标价）。

items.en: Constare meant to stand at a price.
items.cn: constare 意为标价为某个数目。

items.en: Coster meant to cost or be bought for a sum.
items.cn: coster 意为值多少钱、以某价购得。

items.en: English cost named the price of a thing.
items.cn: 英语 cost 指某物的价钱。

items.en: The ending -ly turned it into an adjective of high price.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成表示高价的形容词。

items.en: It now describes both heavy bills and heavy losses.
items.cn: 今天它既形容高额账单，也形容沉重损失。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cost family together, and the meaning group names other words for a high price.
note.cn: 形近组把 cost 家族放在一起，近义组列出其他表示昂贵的说法。

entries.definition: the price paid for something
the work of calculating costs
free of charge
costing a lot of money
high in price in British use
entries.definitionCN: 英式用法中表示价格高的

entries.definition: rather expensive in an informal way

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a thin purse, then move to a victory that hurt and to a repair bill that grows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只瘪钱包开始，再到一场伤人的胜利，最后到不断上涨的维修账单。

normal.en: Cost plus -ly means full of cost, the way friendly means full of friend.
normal.cn: cost 加 -ly 表示满是花费，就像 friendly 表示满是人情。

normal.en: A costly mistake sends its bill months later.
normal.cn: 代价惨重的错误，几个月后才寄来账单。

normal.en: The comparative is costlier, not more costly.
normal.cn: 比较级是 costlier，不是 more costly。

normal.en: A costly victory is a win that feels like a loss.
normal.cn: 惨胜就是一场感觉像失败的胜利。

normal.en: Cheap now, costly later: the same word fits both.
normal.cn: 现在便宜，以后昂贵，同一个词都能形容。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt that grows longer as it falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据往下掉时越变越长。

abstract.en: Picture a trophy with a crack running through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座奖杯上有一道裂纹穿过。

abstract.en: Picture a purse with one coin and one shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包里只有一枚硬币和一道影子。

examples.en: Winning the cup proved costly for the small club.
examples.cn: 赢得奖杯对这家小俱乐部来说代价惨重。

examples.en: The repairs were costly but necessary.
examples.cn: 这次维修很贵，却非做不可。

examples.en: A moment of anger can be the costliest mistake.
examples.cn: 一时的怒气可能成为代价最大的错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 costly 记成 cost（花费）加 ly：处处要花钱，就是昂贵的、代价大的。

root: 由 cost（花费、代价）加形容词词尾 -ly 构成；cost 源自拉丁语 constare（标价），经古法语 coster 而来。

sensesIntro.en: From a high price on a tag, to a loss that never appears on any tag.
sensesIntro.cn: 从价签上的高价，到永远不出现在价签上的损失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wallet opened to show one coin and a long bill.
core.cn: 核心意象：钱包打开，只剩一枚硬币和一张长账单。

branches.en: Money leaves the pocket quickly and visibly.
branches.cn: 钱从口袋离开，又快又看得见。

branches.en: Something precious is lost and the bill is invisible.
branches.cn: 珍贵的东西失去了，账单却看不见。

branches.en: Both uses measure what a thing takes from you.
branches.cn: 两种用法都在衡量一件事从你身上拿走了什么。

branches.en: A costly win can cost health, trust or time.
branches.cn: 代价惨重的胜利，可能搭上健康、信任或时间。

branches.en: The adjective often leans on the word mistake.
branches.cn: 这个形容词常与 mistake 这个词搭配。

intro.en: Costly is a base word plus -ly, an old adjective ending that means having the quality of.
intro.cn: costly 是词根词加 -ly 构成，这个古老形容词词尾表示具有某种性质。

latinIntro.en: The standing base sta- also appears in constant, stable and station.
latinIntro.cn: 表示站立的词基 sta- 也出现在 constant、stable 与 station 中。

items.meaning: price or to have a price

items.exampleCN: 其昂贵程度让他们吃惊。

definition_en: to cook with dry heat, roasted meat, or to tease someone publicly
core_image: 烤箱里慢慢转动的整只鸡
scene: 厨房里，父亲把整只鸡放进烤箱，让它慢慢烤。 In the kitchen, father put the whole chicken in the oven to roast slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 roast 是「烤」（第 1 个义项：用干热烹制食物）；句意：厨房里，父亲把整只鸡放进烤箱，让它慢慢烤。

senses.title: Cooking with dry heat
senses.definition: to cook food with dry heat in an oven or over fire
senses.definitionCN: 在烤箱中或用火以干热烹调食物
senses.example: Roast the nuts for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 把坚果烤十分钟。
senses.why: Dry heat browns and deepens the food.
senses.whyCN: 干热让食物上色并加深风味。

senses.title: Roasted meat
senses.definition: a piece of meat cooked in dry heat
senses.definitionCN: 用干热烹制的一块肉
senses.example: The Sunday roast was wonderful.
senses.exampleCN: 周日的烤肉大餐棒极了。
senses.why: The noun names what the oven has made.
senses.whyCN: 名词指烤箱做出来的东西。

senses.title: Teasing in public
senses.definition: to criticize or joke about someone in a friendly or comic way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好或滑稽的方式公开批评、打趣某人
senses.example: The show roasted a famous actor.
senses.exampleCN: 这档节目公开调侃了一位著名演员。
senses.why: Comedy heat teases without burning.
senses.whyCN: 喜剧的火候，调侃而不灼伤。

intro.en: Roast comes from Old French rostir, to roast.
intro.cn: roast 源自古法语 rostir，意为烤。

items.en: Rostir means to roast over fire.
items.cn: rostir 意为在火上烤。

items.en: Roast enters English as a cooking verb.
items.cn: roast 以烹饪动词之意进入英语。

items.en: The noun names a joint of meat.
items.cn: 名词指一大块烤肉。

items.en: Roast extends to coffee and nuts.
items.cn: roast 扩展到咖啡与坚果。

items.en: The comic roast gives a joking sense.
items.cn: 喜剧调侃节目赋予它开玩笑的义项。

note.en: Roast uses dry heat; boil uses water.
note.cn: roast 用干热，boil 用水。

entries.definition: a pan or machine for roasting
cooked by dry heat
cooking by dry heat
to cook in an oven
to cook under or over strong heat
to brown bread by heat

normalIntro.en: To roast is to let dry heat do the work.
normalIntro.cn: roast 就是让干热来完成工作。

normal.en: Roast beef is a classic Sunday dish.
normal.cn: roast beef 是经典的周日菜肴。

normal.en: Roast chicken fills the kitchen with smell.
normal.cn: roast chicken 让厨房充满香味。

normal.en: Roast potatoes turn golden in the oven.
normal.cn: roast potatoes 在烤箱里变成金黄。

normal.en: A Sunday roast brings the family together.
normal.cn: a Sunday roast 让一家人聚在一起。

normal.en: To roast a friend is to tease them kindly.
normal.cn: roast 朋友就是善意地打趣。

abstract.en: Picture a chicken turning slowly above coals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸡在炭火上慢慢转动。

abstract.en: Imagine the kitchen warm and full of steam.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房温暖、蒸汽弥漫。

abstract.en: Think of a comedian's gentle fire on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象喜剧演员在台上燃起的温和之火。

examples.en: We roasted vegetables for dinner.
examples.cn: 我们烤了蔬菜当晚餐。

examples.en: He ordered the roast with potatoes.
examples.cn: 他点了烤肉配土豆。

examples.en: The comic roasted the whole team.
examples.cn: 这位喜剧演员把整支队伍都调侃了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roast」听起来像「热死它」——用热力把它烘透，就是烤。

root: 古法语 rostir（在火上烤）→ roast，核心义「用干热使食物变熟上色」，再引申出公开「烤」人的调侃义。

sensesIntro.en: Roast means to cook with dry heat, the meat so cooked, or to tease someone publicly.
sensesIntro.cn: roast 意为用干热烹调、这样烤出的肉，或公开调侃某人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dry heat browning food.
core.cn: 核心意象：干热让食物上色。

branches.en: Cooking with dry heat is the core sense.
branches.cn: 干热烹制是核心义项。

branches.en: The noun names the finished meat.
branches.cn: 名词指烤好的肉。

branches.en: Comic teasing borrows the heat image.
branches.cn: 喜剧调侃借用了热度意象。

branches.en: The verb and its product share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与其产物共用一个词。

branches.en: Both real fire and comic fire need good control.
branches.cn: 真实的火与喜剧的火都需要掌控火候。

intro.en: Roast is a French borrowing from rostir.
intro.cn: roast 是来自 rostir 的法语借词。

latinIntro.en: The French verb is its direct parent.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词是它的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指一种传统。

definition_en: in a strong and determined way, or in a way that does not move
core_image: 锤子落下，钉子稳稳扎进木板
scene: 她把钉子牢牢地敲进木板。 She hammered the nail firmly into the board.
sceneCN: 这里 firmly 是「牢固地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她把钉子牢牢地敲进木板。

senses.title: With determination
senses.definition: in a strong and determined way
senses.definitionCN: 以坚强、果断的方式
senses.example: She firmly believes in second chances.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚定地相信人应该有第二次机会。
senses.why: This sense describes resolve.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项描述决心。

senses.title: Securely in place
senses.definition: in a way that is solid and does not move
senses.definitionCN: 以稳固、不会移动的方式
senses.example: She hammered the nail firmly into the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钉子牢牢地敲进木板。
senses.why: This sense describes physical steadiness.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项描述物理上的稳固。

intro.en: Firmly is firm plus the adverb suffix -ly, so it carries the history of Latin firmus.

items.en: Ferme meant solid and steadfast.

items.en: Firm meant solid and unyielding.

entries.definition: solid or steady
at last
in a delicate way
with firm determination

in a close or firm way

normalIntro.cn: firmly 说明动作是以力量完成的，或做到纹丝不动。

normal.en: Hold the rope firmly.

normal.en: The lid was firmly closed.

normal.en: The tree is firmly rooted.
normal.cn: 这棵树根扎得很牢。

normal.en: He firmly believes in practice.

abstract.en: To stand firmly is to choose not to be moved.
abstract.cn: 稳稳站住，就是选择不被移动。

abstract.en: A grip and a promise can both be firm.
abstract.cn: 握持与承诺，都可以是牢固的。

abstract.en: What is firmly rooted survives the wind.
abstract.cn: 根扎得牢的东西，能挺过风。

examples.en: She hammered the nail firmly into the board.
examples.cn: 她把钉子牢牢地敲进木板。

branches.en: Acting with clear resolve.

branches.en: Fixing something so it stays.
branches.cn: 把某物固定住。

definition_en: a pile of things, or a large number or amount
core_image: 墙角落叶越堆越高，成了一座小山
scene: 落叶在墙角堆成一大堆。 The fallen leaves made a heap in the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 heap 是「堆」（第 1 个义项）；句意：落叶在墙角堆成一大堆。

senses.title: A pile
senses.definition: a pile of things lying on top of one another
senses.definitionCN: 层层叠放着的一堆东西
senses.example: The fallen leaves made a heap in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶在墙角堆成一大堆。
senses.why: This is the shape you can see.
senses.whyCN: 这是眼睛能看到的形状。

senses.title: A lot

senses.definitionCN: 数量很多的某物
senses.example: She has heaps of work today.
senses.exampleCN: 她今天有一大堆工作。
senses.why: A pile of things becomes a pile of work.

intro.en: Heap comes from Old English heap, a pile or crowd.
intro.cn: heap 来自古英语 heap，意为堆或人群。

items.en: Heap meant a pile or a troop.
items.cn: heap 指一堆东西或一群人。

items.en: Related forms named a crowd or mound.
items.cn: 同源形式表示人群或土丘。

items.en: The word settled on a pile of things.
items.cn: 词义固定为一堆物品。

items.en: Heaps of came to mean a lot of.
items.cn: heaps of 开始表示大量。

items.en: The scrap heap named things thrown away.
items.cn: scrap heap 指被丢弃的废料堆。

note.en: Heap is compared with look-alike words and with words for a pile.

entries.definition: high temperature
to make things easier for someone
the side of the body below the waist
things stacked together
a neat pile
a small hill or pile

normalIntro.en: Heap is a pile you can point at, and then a lot you cannot count.
normalIntro.cn: heap 是能用手指的一堆，接着又成了数不清的大量。

normal.en: A heap of books sat on the floor.
normal.cn: 地板上放着一堆书。

normal.en: He left his clothes in a heap.
normal.cn: 他把衣服堆成一团。

normal.en: We have heaps of time.
normal.cn: 我们时间很充裕。

normal.en: The old car went to the scrap heap.
normal.cn: 那辆旧车进了废料堆。

normal.en: She is at the top of the heap.
normal.cn: 她处在最顶尖的位置。

abstract.en: A heap is order giving up for a moment.
abstract.cn: 一堆，是秩序暂时放弃了抵抗。

abstract.en: Small things gather until they become a landscape.
abstract.cn: 小东西聚着聚着，就成了风景。

abstract.en: The scrap heap is where old stories wait.
abstract.cn: 废料堆是旧故事等待的地方。

examples.en: The books lay in a heap by the door.
examples.cn: 书在门边堆成一堆。

dict_mnemonic.text: heap 就是「堆」；看得见的一堆东西是 heap，看不见的一堆事情就是 heaps of work，废料堆是 scrap heap。

root: 来自古英语 heap（堆、人群），属日耳曼语词；由实物的堆叠，引申为数量上的「大量」，并固定出 scrap heap、top of the heap 等说法。

sensesIntro.en: Heap begins as a visible pile and widens into a large amount.
sensesIntro.cn: heap 从看得见的一堆开始，扩展为数量上的大量。

core.en: A corner filling up with fallen leaves.

branches.en: Clothes lie where they were dropped.
branches.cn: 衣服落在脱下时的地方。

branches.en: A pile of things becomes a pile of chores.
branches.cn: 一堆东西，变成一堆杂事。

branches.en: Heaps of time feel like no time at all.

intro.en: Heap forms a plural, adjective forms, and common phrases.
intro.cn: heap 有复数、形容词形式，也构成常见短语。

definition_en: to remove impurities from a substance; to improve something by small careful changes; to make manners or taste more polished
core_image: 糖浆在铜锅里慢慢熬成雪白的结晶
scene: 糖厂的铜锅冒着热气，浓稠的糖浆被一遍遍撇去浮沫。 The plant refines raw sugar before it reaches the shops.
sceneCN: 这里 refines 是 refine 的第三人称单数，取「提炼」（第 1 个义项：除去杂质使物质纯净）；句意为工厂先把粗糖提炼，再送进商店。画面里可留意：冒热气的铜锅、被撇去的浮沫。

senses.title: To purify a substance
senses.definition: to remove impurities from oil, sugar, or metal
senses.definitionCN: 除去油、糖或金属中的杂质
senses.example: The plant refines raw sugar before it reaches the shops.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂先把粗糖提炼，再送进商店。
senses.why: Fine here means pure, and the prefix says the work is done again and again until the last impurity is gone.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 fine 意为纯净，前缀则表示这道工序要反复进行，直到最后一点杂质也被除去。

senses.title: To improve by small changes
senses.definition: to make a method, design, or skill better through careful adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 通过细致的调整使方法、设计或技能更好
senses.example: The team spent a month refining the test before the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在发布前花了一个月改进这项测试。
senses.why: Improving a method is a slow filtering of ideas: each round removes what does not work.
senses.whyCN: 改良方法是对想法进行缓慢的过滤：每一轮都去掉行不通的部分。

senses.title: To make polished
senses.definition: to make manners, taste, or language more delicate and cultivated
senses.definitionCN: 使举止、品味或语言更细腻有教养
senses.example: Years abroad had refined her taste in music.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的海外生活使她的音乐品味变得精细。
senses.why: The same word moves from metal to manners: what is refined has been worked over until the coarse part is gone.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从金属转到举止：凡被 refined 的东西，都是经过反复打磨，粗陋之处已去。

intro.en: Refine is to make fine: the Latin limit becomes a finish, and repeated finishing removes what is coarse.
intro.cn: refine 就是「使精细」：拉丁语的「界限」变成了「完工」，而反复的精加工去掉了粗糙之处。

items.en: Finis meant an end, a limit, or a boundary, and it grew into words about finishing and fineness.
items.cn: finis 意为终点、界限或边界，由此生长出关于「完成」与「精细」的词。

items.en: French affiner meant to make fine or pure, built on fin, the same root as finis.
items.cn: 法语 affiner 意为使精细或纯净，其词根 fin 与 finis 同源。

items.en: Middle French raffiner added the prefix of repetition to affiner and named the purifying of sugar and metal.
items.cn: 中期法语 raffiner 在 affiner 前加上表重复的前缀，用来指炼糖与炼金属。

items.en: English borrowed the word for purifying substances and soon extended it to improving anything.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词表示提纯物质，很快又扩展到改进任何事物。

items.en: The sense of polished manners grew in the eighteenth century, when taste itself was thought of as something to be refined.
items.cn: 「举止文雅」这一义在十八世纪发展起来，那时品味本身也被视为可以精炼的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin finis; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of purifying and improving.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁 finis 构成的词；近义组收表示提纯与改进的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word says make fine: take a coarse thing and work it until only the fine part is left.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的意思是「使精细」：拿一件粗糙的东西反复加工，直到只剩精细的部分。

normal.en: Re plus fine: to make something fine again and again.
normal.cn: re 加 fine：反复把某物做得更精细。

normal.en: A refinery is the place where crude oil is refined.
normal.cn: refinery 就是原油被提炼的地方。

normal.en: Refine a method means to take out the steps that do not work.
normal.cn: refine a method 指去掉行不通的步骤。

normal.en: Refined sugar is white; refined manners are smooth.
normal.cn: 精炼的糖是白的，文雅的举止是顺的。

normal.en: The noun is refinement, the adjective refined.
normal.cn: 名词是 refinement，形容词是 refined。

abstract.en: Refining is less about adding than about removing.
abstract.cn: 精炼与其说是添加，不如说是去除。

abstract.en: A person is refined by what they have learned to leave out.
abstract.cn: 一个人之所以文雅，在于学会了舍弃什么。

abstract.en: Every craft improves by small refinements no one notices.
abstract.cn: 每一门手艺都靠无人注意的细小改良而进步。

examples.en: The team spent a month refining the test before the launch.
examples.cn: 团队在发布前花了一个月改进这项测试。

examples.en: Years abroad had refined her taste in music.
examples.cn: 多年的海外生活使她的音乐品味变得精细。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（反复）加 fine（精细）：反复地弄精细，就是提炼杂质、改进方法、打磨举止。

root: 拉丁 finis（界限、终点）→ 法语 affiner（使精细）→ 中期法语 raffiner → 英语 refine；同族有 refinement、refinery，形近的 define、confine、finish 也出自 finis。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making fine; the senses move from removing impurities in matter, to improving a method by small steps, to polishing manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使精细」；义项从除去物质中的杂质，到以小步改进方法，再到打磨举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick syrup in a copper pan slowly turning into white crystals.
core.cn: 核心意象：铜锅里的浓糖浆慢慢熬成雪白的结晶。

branches.en: white sugar in a paper bag
branches.cn: 纸袋里的白糖

branches.en: a test rewritten five times
branches.cn: 改了五遍的测试

branches.en: a quiet, well-chosen compliment
branches.cn: 一句克制而得体的赞美

branches.en: impurities taken out of a process
branches.cn: 从流程中剔除杂质

branches.en: a sharpened skill and a softened manner
branches.cn: 更精的技术与更柔的举止

intro.en: A Latin word for a boundary turns into a verb of finishing, and the prefix of repetition turns finishing into refining.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表「边界」的词转成表「完成」的动词，表重复的前缀又把「完成」变成「精炼」。

latinIntro.en: The base is finis, a limit or end, which also gives the Latin verb finire, to finish.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 finis（界限、终点），它也给出拉丁动词 finire（完成）。

definition_zh: 使精疲力尽；耗尽；废气；排气管
definition_en: to make very tired, to use something up completely, or the waste gas from an engine
core_image: 被抽干的一口井
scene: 跑完马拉松后，他精疲力尽地倒在草地上。 After the marathon he was exhausted and fell onto the grass.
sceneCN: 这里 exhaust 是「使精疲力尽」（第 1 个义项）；句意：跑完马拉松后，他精疲力尽地倒在草地上。

senses.title: Make very tired
senses.definition: to make someone feel extremely tired
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到极度疲惫
senses.example: The long climb exhausted the whole group.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的攀爬让整队人精疲力尽。
senses.why: Energy is drawn out until little is left.
senses.whyCN: 能量被抽走，所剩无几。

senses.title: Use up
senses.definition: to use something until none is left
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物直到一点都不剩
senses.example: The country exhausted its oil reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家耗尽了石油储备。
senses.why: The well is pumped dry.
senses.whyCN: 水井被抽干。

senses.title: Waste gas
senses.definition: the gas or pipe that carries burned fuel away from an engine
senses.definitionCN: 发动机排出的废气，或输送废气的管道
senses.example: The truck poured black exhaust into the air.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车把黑色废气排到空气中。
senses.why: What is drawn out of the engine is pushed away.
senses.whyCN: 从发动机里抽出的东西被排走。

intro.en: Exhaust comes from Latin exhaurire, to draw water out.
intro.cn: exhaust 源自拉丁语 exhaurire，意为把水抽出。

items.en: Haurire means to draw water.
items.cn: haurire 意为汲水。

items.cn: exhaurire 由 ex-（出）与 haurire（汲）组成。

items.cn: exhaurire 意为抽干水井或花光财产。

items.en: English exhaust keeps the image of drawing dry.
items.cn: 英语 exhaust 保留抽干的意象。

items.en: Exhaust also names the gas from an engine.
items.cn: exhaust 又用来指发动机排出的气体。

note.en: Exhausted means drained; exhaustive means complete.
note.cn: exhausted 是被抽干、精疲力尽，exhaustive 则是彻底的。

abstract.cn: 想象烟从管子里冒出并飘散。

examples.cn: 高温让大厅里所有人都疲惫不堪。

examples.en: Years of mining exhausted the hills.
examples.cn: 多年开采耗尽了这些山丘的资源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ haust（抽）」——把水和力气都抽出去，人就精疲力尽，资源也用光；剩下的废气也被排出去。

branches.en: Tiredness and empty supplies share the drain.

branches.en: What is taken out must also go somewhere.

intro.en: Exhaust combines ex-, out, with Latin haurire, to draw water.

latinIntro.en: Exhaurire becomes exhaustus and then English exhaust.

latinEntries.example: Exhaurire is the source of exhaust.

senses.definition: as well as something else

definition_zh: 或者；作为另一种选择；（提出另一种解释）也可能
definition_en: used to introduce another possibility, either a different course of action or a different explanation
core_image: 写到一半的方案页边，用铅笔补了一条「或者」
scene: 出发前她看了看天气，说可以坐地铁，或者干脆改天再去。 We could go now; alternatively, we could wait until tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 alternatively 是「或者」（第 1 个义项：提出另一条可选的做法）；句意是我们现在可以去，或者等到明天。

senses.title: As another course of action
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to offer a different action that could be taken instead
senses.definitionCN: 置于分句开头，提出可以改做的另一件事
senses.example: We could walk; alternatively, we could take the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以走过去，或者坐公交。
senses.why: The adverb is alternative turned into a sentence connector, so it points from the action just named to the other action on offer.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 alternative 变来的句子连接词，作用是从刚提到的做法指向另一个可选做法。

senses.title: As another explanation
senses.titleCN: 也可能是；另一种解释是
senses.definition: used to offer a second possible explanation for the same facts
senses.definitionCN: 针对同样的事实提出第二种可能的解释
senses.example: The delay may be due to traffic; alternatively, the driver may be lost.
senses.exampleCN: 延误可能是堵车，也可能是司机迷路了。
senses.why: The same connector works for ideas as well as actions: when the alternatives are explanations rather than plans, it introduces a rival account of the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个连接词同样可用于想法而不只是行动：当备选项是解释而不是计划时，它引出对同一证据的另一种说法。

scene: 老茶馆里，几位老人围着方桌，其中一位拍着桌沿要讲往事。 He told a funny anecdote about his first day at work.
sceneCN: 这里 anecdote 是「轶事、趣闻」（第 1 个义项：关于真人真事的短小故事）；句意为讲了一件关于他上班第一天的趣事。画面里有茶壶、方桌与围坐的老人。

pos.zh: 名词：轶事；趣闻；秘闻；插叙故事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「轶事的；传闻式的」
anecdotal 加 -ly 构成，义为「据轶闻所说；以传闻方式」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「爱讲轶事的人」

senses.title: A short amusing story about real people
senses.titleCN: 轶事：关于真人真事的短故事
senses.definition: a short story about a real incident or person, usually amusing and told to make a point
senses.definitionCN: 关于真实事件或人物的短故事，通常有趣，用来说明某个观点
senses.example: He opened the lecture with an anecdote about his grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一则关于祖父的轶事开场。
senses.why: Greek anekdota meant 'things not published'; the word still carries the flavour of something told rather than printed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anekdota 意为「未发表的东西」，这个词至今仍带着「口耳相传而非刊印」的味道。

senses.title: A piece of unpublished gossip
senses.titleCN: 秘闻：未公开的内幕细节
senses.definition: a small, often private detail about a public person or event that is repeated informally
senses.definitionCN: 关于公众人物或事件、常在私下流传的细小私密细节
senses.example: The biography is full of anecdotes about the minister's temper.
senses.exampleCN: 这本传记满是关于那位部长脾气的秘闻。
senses.why: The original Greek title described secret history; the modern sense keeps that whiff of the not-quite-official.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原题指「秘史」，现代义仍保留那一点「不太官方」的气息。

senses.title: A digression inside a longer work
senses.titleCN: 插叙：长篇作品中的小故事
senses.definition: a short digression or illustrative story inserted into a speech, essay or longer narrative
senses.definitionCN: 插入演讲、文章或较长叙事中的简短插叙或说明性故事
senses.example: The essay uses an anecdote to break up a long argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章用一则小故事打断冗长的论证。
senses.why: In writing, the anecdote works as a pause: a small real scene dropped into the middle of abstract argument.
senses.whyCN: 在写作中，轶事起到停顿作用：把一个真实的小场景放进抽象论证的中间。

intro.en: Anecdote began as the title of a secret history and became the name of any small telling story.
intro.cn: anecdote 起初是一部秘史的书名，后来变成任何短小讲述故事的名称。

items.en: Anekdota meant 'things not published', from an- 'not' and ekdidonai 'to publish out'.
items.cn: anekdota 意为「未发表的东西」，由 an-「不」与 ekdidonai「发表出去」构成。

items.en: The historian Procopius gave the title Anekdota to his secret account of the emperor Justinian's court.
items.cn: 史家普罗科匹厄斯把自己关于查士丁尼宫廷的秘史题为 Anekdota。

items.en: French turned the title into a common noun for a short unpublished detail, and English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语把这个书名转为普通名词，指未公开的细小细节，英语再借入。

items.en: English anecdote first meant a secret detail of history; the modern 'short amusing story' sense grew later.
items.cn: 英语 anecdote 最初指历史的隐秘细节；现代「有趣的短故事」义是后来长出来的。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word had softened from secret history into the everyday telling of a small incident.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词已从秘史软化为日常讲述的一件小事。

items.en: Today an anecdote is welcome in speeches and essays, valued for being concrete rather than statistical.
items.cn: 如今轶事在演讲与文章中受欢迎，价值在于具体，而不在统计。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anecdote family; the near-meaning group holds kinds of short narrative.
note.cn: 形近组是 anecdote 词族；近义组收各类短小叙事。

entries.definition: Based on personal stories rather than systematic evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 基于个人讲述而非系统证据的。

entries.definition: In the manner of an anecdote, or according to stories rather than data.
entries.definitionCN: 以轶事的方式，或依据传闻而非数据。

entries.definition: A person fond of telling anecdotes.
The general word for a told account of events, true or invented.
entries.definitionCN: 叙述事件的通用词，无论真实或虚构。

entries.definition: A story, often one that is old, invented or slightly exaggerated.
entries.definitionCN: 故事，常指古老的、虚构的或略有夸张的。

entries.definition: A factual report of what happened.
entries.definitionCN: 对所发生之事的纪实性叙述。

entries.definition: A short piece of writing or drama, lighter than a full story.
entries.definitionCN: 短小的文章或戏剧片段，比完整故事轻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to its Greek secret title, its sound, and the picture of a table of listeners.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与希腊语「秘史」书名、读音以及一桌听众的画面连起来。

normal.en: The an- at the front means not, and the rest once meant published: an anecdote began as an unpublished thing.
normal.cn: 开头的 an- 表示「不」，其余部分曾表示「发表」：anecdote 起初是「未发表的东西」。

normal.en: Say 'AN-ik-dote': three beats, like a short story told in three breaths.
normal.cn: 读作「AN-尼克-兜特」，三拍，像用三口讲完的小故事。

normal.en: Picture a circle of chairs and one person leaning forward to begin.
normal.cn: 想象一圈椅子，一个人俯身向前开始讲。

normal.en: Anecdote and antidote differ by one letter: one cures boredom, the other cures poison.
normal.cn: anecdote 与 antidote 只差一个字母：一个治无聊，一个解毒。

normal.en: The adjective anecdotal is the warning label: stories are not data.
normal.cn: 形容词 anecdotal 是警告标签：故事不等于数据。

abstract.en: An anecdote is a small door through which a large idea can enter a room.
abstract.cn: 轶事是一扇小门，宏大的想法可以由此进入一间屋子。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that unpublished things are often the most alive.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们：未发表的东西往往最有生命力。

abstract.en: Every anecdote is a claim that one small scene can stand for a wider truth.
abstract.cn: 每一则轶事都在声称：一个小场景可以代表更广的真相。

examples.en: The teacher told an anecdote about a student who became a pilot.
examples.cn: 老师讲了一则关于一名学生后来成为飞行员的故事。

examples.en: His speech was full of anecdotes but short on evidence.
examples.cn: 他的演讲满是轶事，却缺少证据。

examples.en: She kept a notebook of anecdotes for future lectures.
examples.cn: 她记了一本轶事笔记，留着以后讲课用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安尼克抖特」：安尼克抖着腿讲了一段小趣闻，逗得大家笑。

root: 希腊语 an-（不）+ ekdidonai（发表），anekdota 即「未发表的东西」，原为一部秘史的书名。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from secret history to any short telling story, then to private gossip and to the digression inside a longer work.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从秘史走到任何短小讲述的故事，再到私下流传的秘闻，以及长篇中的插叙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small real incident pulled out of the flow of time and told across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：从时间长河里抽出一件真实小事，在桌边讲给人听。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the first sense is the everyday telling of a small true story.
branches.cn: 茶桌线：第一个义项是日常讲述一件真实小事的本事。

branches.en: THE SECRET: the second sense keeps the original flavour of the unpublished detail.
branches.cn: 秘闻线：第二个义项保留「未公开细节」的原味。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the third sense places the small story inside a larger argument.
branches.cn: 书页线：第三个义项把小故事放进更大的论证里。

branches.en: THE ILLUSTRATION: both spoken and written anecdotes exist to make a point concrete.
branches.cn: 说明线：口讲与书写的轶事都是为了让观点变具体。

branches.en: THE DIGRESSION: gossip and inserted stories both interrupt the main line on purpose.
branches.cn: 插曲线：秘闻与插叙都故意打断主线。

intro.en: English builds the family with -al, -ally and -ist, and the stem remains anecdotal- before most suffixes.
intro.cn: 英语用 -al、-ally、-ist 扩展这个词族，多数后缀前的词干为 anecdotal-。

latinIntro.en: The Greek stem anekdot- reached English through French; the suffixes are English additions.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词干 anekdot- 经法语进入英语，后缀都是英语后来添加的。

items.meaning: based on personal stories rather than proof
items.meaningCN: 基于个人讲述而非证据的

items.meaning: by way of stories or reports
items.example: Anecdotally, the remedy seems to help.
items.exampleCN: 据传闻，这个疗法似乎有帮助。

items.example: The old captain was a born anecdotist.
items.exampleCN: 这位老船长天生爱讲轶事。

items.meaning: evidence made of stories, not measurements
items.meaningCN: 由故事而非测量构成的证据
items.example: Anecdotal evidence is easy to collect and hard to trust.
items.exampleCN: 轶闻证据容易收集，却难以信任。

items.meaning: a short story from one's own life
items.meaningCN: 来自本人生活的小故事
items.example: He opened with a personal anecdote.
items.exampleCN: 他以一则个人轶事开场。

items.meaning: a story repeated within a family
items.meaningCN: 家族内部反复讲述的故事
items.example: That family anecdote gets longer every year.
items.exampleCN: 那则家族轶事每年都变得更长。

items.meaning: a gathered set of short stories
items.example: The volume is an anecdote collection rather than a history.
items.exampleCN: 这卷书是轶事集，而不是史书。

items.meaning: history told through small personal stories
items.meaningCN: 通过个人小故事讲述的历史
items.example: The book offers an anecdotal history of the street.
items.exampleCN: 这本书提供了一条街的轶事史。

definition_zh: 整齐地；有条理地；干净利落地；简洁地
definition_en: in a way that leaves everything tidy and in place; skilfully and with precision; briefly and clearly
core_image: 衬衫按颜色叠成同样大小的方块，一层层摞进抽屉
scene: 衣柜的抽屉拉开，衬衫按颜色叠成方块，袜子卷成同样大小的卷。 She neatly folded the sheets and stacked them on the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里是「整齐地」（第 1 个义项：动作的结果井然有序）；句意为她把床单叠得整整齐齐，摞在架子上。图中可辨识物件：抽屉、衬衫、袜子卷。

pos.zh: 整齐地；有条理地；干净利落地；简洁地

derivatives.zh: neatly 的词根，义为「整洁的；简洁的」
由 neat 加 -ness 构成，义为「整洁；工整」
由 neat 加 -en 构成，义为「把……收拾整齐」

senses.title: In a tidy and orderly way
senses.definition: in a way that puts everything in its proper place and leaves no clutter
senses.definitionCN: 以各物归位、不留杂乱的方式做事
senses.example: She neatly folded the sheets and stacked them on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 她把床单叠得整整齐齐，摞在架子上。
senses.why: Neat describes the finished state of a surface, and the ending -ly turns that state into the manner of the action that produced it, so neatly always points at how the hands worked.
senses.whyCN: neat 描述表面的完成状态，词尾 -ly 把这种状态变成造成它的动作方式，所以 neatly 总是指向双手怎么做的。

senses.title: Skilfully and with precision
senses.definition: in a careful, exact and efficient way, so that the result looks effortless and simple
senses.definitionCN: 以细致、准确、高效的方式，使结果显得轻松而简单
senses.example: He neatly solved the problem in three lines.
senses.exampleCN: 他用三行就干净利落地解决了这个问题。
senses.why: When a task is done with nothing wasted, the result has the same bare cleanness as a tidy desk, so the adverb of order also praises economy of effort.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得没有半点浪费，结果就带着和整洁桌面一样的干净，于是这个表示「有序」的副词也用来称赞省力。

senses.title: Briefly and clearly
senses.definition: in a short and well-organized way, used of speech, writing or a summary
senses.definitionCN: 以简短而有条理的方式，用于说话、写作或概述
senses.example: The report neatly sums up a year of work in two pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告用两页纸把一年的工作简明扼要地总结了。
senses.why: Writing that keeps only what is needed looks like a room with only what is needed, so neatly moves from furniture to sentences without changing its judgement.
senses.whyCN: 只留下必需内容的文章，看起来就像只摆必需家具的房间，于是 neatly 从家具移到句子，判断标准却一点没变。

intro.en: Neatly is the adjective of cleanliness turned into an adverb of manner, and its history is the history of neat plus the English -ly.
intro.cn: neatly 是把表示「干净」的形容词变成方式副词的产物，它的历史就是 neat 加上英语词尾 -ly 的历史。

items.en: Nitidus meant shining and polished, and it reached French with the sense of something clean and unspoiled.
items.cn: nitidus 意为光亮、打磨过的，传到法语时带着「干净、未受损」的意思。

items.en: Old French net described clean cloth, clear writing and a neat appearance, and English borrowed it in that shape.
items.cn: 古法语 net 形容干净的布、清楚的字迹与整洁的外表，英语就是照这个形态借入的。

items.en: Middle English neat named the quality of a well-kept thing, and the adverb was formed by adding the ending for manner.
items.cn: 中古英语 neat 指收拾得好的事物所具有的性质，副词则由加上表示方式的词尾构成。

items.en: The old ending -lice became -ly, and it turned adjectives of state into adverbs of how an action is carried out.
items.cn: 旧词尾 -lice 变成 -ly，把表示状态的形容词变成说明动作如何进行的副词。

items.en: Modern English uses neatly for folding, dressing, writing and solving, keeping one adverb for every kind of visible order.
items.cn: 现代英语把 neatly 用于叠衣、穿衣、书写与解题，各种看得见的秩序都用同一个副词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds neat and the words formed on it; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs of careful, orderly execution.
note.cn: 形近组收 neat 以及建在它上面的词；近义组收其他表示「仔细、有序地做事」的副词。

entries.definition: Tidy, simple or undiluted, the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁的、简洁的或纯的，是副词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality that neatly describes when it appears in an action.
entries.definitionCN: neatly 所描述的那种性质本身。

entries.definition: To make something tidy, formed with -en.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物收拾整齐；由 neat 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: Shining and polished, a learned word from the same Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 光亮而打磨过的，是同出拉丁形容词的书面罕用词。

entries.definition: With everything put away, said of rooms and possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西都收好，多用于房间与物品。

entries.definition: Without mess or awkwardness, often of a cut or a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不拖泥带水，常用于切口或动作。

entries.definition: With exact measurement or exact wording, stressing accuracy.
entries.definitionCN: 以精确的度量或措辞，强调准确。

entries.definition: Step by step in a fixed order, stressing the plan rather than the look.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定顺序一步步来，强调计划而非外观。

normalIntro.en: The word is neat with the manner ending -ly, so it names the way an action produces order rather than the order itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 neat 加表示方式的词尾 -ly，所以它命名的是动作造成秩序的方式，而不是秩序本身。

normal.en: Neat is the adjective and neatly the adverb: a neat shelf, but she stacked them neatly.
normal.cn: neat 是形容词，neatly 是副词：说 a neat shelf，但说 she stacked them neatly。

normal.en: The ending -ly goes back to Old English -lice, which meant in the manner of.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 可追到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。

normal.en: Neatly keeps the clean-surface idea of neat, so a neatly solved problem has no wasted steps.
normal.cn: neatly 保留了 neat 的「干净表面」之意，所以 a neatly solved problem 没有多余步骤。

normal.en: Neatly folded and neatly dressed both describe how the result looks to someone standing nearby.
normal.cn: neatly folded 与 neatly dressed 都在描述结果在旁人眼里是什么样子。

normal.en: In writing, neatly means briefly and in order, the same standard applied to sentences instead of shelves.
normal.cn: 在写作里，neatly 意为简短而有条理，只是把同一标准从架子用到句子上。

abstract.en: An adverb of tidiness is really a report on the hands: it says the work left nothing loose behind.
abstract.cn: 一个表示整洁的副词，其实是对双手的报告：它说这件活没留下任何松散之处。

abstract.en: Order can be folded into a drawer, solved on a blackboard, or compressed into two pages, and the same word follows it.
abstract.cn: 秩序可以叠进抽屉、写在黑板上，也可以压进两页纸，同一个词一路跟着它。

abstract.en: Neatly is neat seen from the side of the action, which is why it always answers the question of how.
abstract.cn: neatly 是从动作那一侧看到的 neat，所以它回答的总是「怎么做」。

examples.en: The towels were neatly stacked in the cupboard.
examples.cn: 毛巾整齐地摞在柜子里。

examples.en: She neatly avoided the question and moved on.
examples.cn: 她巧妙地避开那个问题，继续往下说。

examples.en: Everything on the desk was neatly arranged by size.
examples.cn: 桌上的每样东西都按大小排列得整整齐齐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼特利」——手脚利落，东西摆得整齐；neatly 就是整齐地。

root: 由 neat（整洁的，源自法语 net、拉丁语 nitidus）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；本义「以干净整洁的方式」，后引申出「利落地」「简洁地」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the manner of producing order; folding, solving and writing are three places where that manner can be seen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「造成秩序的方式」；叠衣、解题与写作，是这种方式可以显现的三个场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shirts folded into identical squares and laid in layers inside a drawer.
core.cn: 核心意象：衬衫叠成同样大小的方块，一层层放进抽屉。

branches.en: sheets folded into one flat stack
branches.cn: 叠成一摞平整的床单

branches.en: socks rolled to the same size
branches.cn: 卷成同样大小的袜子

branches.en: three lines that finish a long proof
branches.cn: 三行就结束的冗长证明

branches.en: a problem closed without a stray mark
branches.cn: 做完后没有多余笔迹的题

branches.en: two pages that hold a whole year
branches.cn: 两页纸装下一整年

intro.en: The word is the cleanliness adjective of French and Latin origin plus the English manner ending that turned it into an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是源自法语与拉丁语、表示「干净」的形容词，加上把它变成副词的英语方式词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin nitidus and its verb nitere stand behind the French adjective, and the English adverb adds only a manner ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nitidus 及其动词 nitere 位于法语形容词之后，英语副词只再加一个方式词尾。

items.meaning: in a tidy or skilful way

latinEntries.meaningCN: 光亮的；打磨过的；整洁的

definition_en: coming after the nine hundred and ninety-ninth in order, or one of a thousand equal parts
core_image: 一条刻满小格的长尺，第一千格恰好是最后一格
scene: 计时器屏幕上数字飞速滚动,终于停在一个极小的刻度上。 His final run was decided by a thousandth of a second.
sceneCN: 这里 thousandth 是「千分之一」（第 2 个义项：一千等分之一）；句意为他的最后一跑以千分之一秒之差决出胜负。

forms.label: 小数读法中的分数用法

derivatives.zh: 去掉序数后缀 -th 得到的基数词，义为「一千」
由基数词加 -fold 构成，义为「千倍的」
基数词的复数，义为「数以千计」

senses.title: The one in position one thousand
senses.definition: coming after the nine hundred and ninety-ninth in a series or order
senses.definitionCN: 在序列中排在第九百九十九之后
senses.example: The thousandth visitor to the museum received a small gift.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的第一千位访客收到了一份小礼物。
senses.why: The ordinal -th simply marks a position in the long counting line.
senses.whyCN: 序数后缀 -th 只是标出这条长长计数线上的一个位置。

senses.title: One of a thousand equal parts
senses.definition: one of a thousand equal divisions of a whole, especially of a unit of measurement
senses.definitionCN: 把一个整体等分成一千份中的一份，尤用于计量单位
senses.example: The lens is polished to within a thousandth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这块镜片被磨到误差不超过千分之一毫米。
senses.why: Once the word names the thousandth place, it doubles as a very small fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦命名第一千格，也就兼任极小分数的角色。

senses.title: For the last time in a long count
senses.definition: in phrases such as the thousandth time, used to mean far too many times
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the thousandth time 等短语，表示次数多到不胜其烦
senses.example: For the thousandth time, please close the window.
senses.exampleCN: 我都说过一千次了，请把窗户关上。
senses.why: The exact ordinal turns into a speaker’s exasperation, an exaggeration for endless repetition.
senses.whyCN: 精确的序数词变成说话人的恼火，是对无尽重复的夸张说法。

intro.en: Thousandth is thousand plus the ordinary English ordinal ending -th, exactly as fourth and fifth are made.
intro.cn: thousandth 就是 thousand 加英语常见的序数后缀 -th，与 fourth、fifth 构词方式完全相同。

items.en: The base is the old compound meaning a great hundred, discussed under thousand.
items.cn: 词基就是表示「大百」的古老复合词，详见 thousand 条目。

items.en: Old English already had the ordinal of the large counting word, marking a position in a long series.
items.cn: 古英语已有这个大写计数词的序数形式，用来标记长序列中的一个位置。

items.en: Middle English dropped the old irregular ordinal endings and extended -th to most numerals.
items.cn: 中古英语淘汰了古老的不规则序数词尾，把 -th 推广到绝大多数数词。

items.en: By early modern English the spelling thousandth was fixed, both for order and for the fraction.
items.cn: 到早期现代英语，thousandth 的拼写已经固定，既表顺序也表分数。

items.en: Science popularised the fractional use, since a thousandth of a unit is a useful very small measure.
items.cn: 科学计量推广了它的分数用法，因为一个单位的千分之一是很有用的极小量。

note.en: The first group lines up ordinal neighbours; the second compares small fractions and large counts.
note.cn: 第一组排开相邻的序数词；第二组比较小分数与大数量。

entries.definition: The ordinal of hundred, with the same -th ending.
The ordinal of million, one step further up the scale.
entries.definitionCN: 百万的序数词，在刻度上再进一档

entries.definition: The ordinal of ten; -th after a vowel sound behaves differently.
entries.definitionCN: 十的序数词；接元音后时 -th 的读音不同

entries.definition: The cardinal form, one thousand.
A part of a whole number; the general word that thousandth is one kind of.
entries.definitionCN: 分数；千分之一属于其中的一类

entries.definition: A number written with a point, such as nought point nought nought one for a thousandth.
entries.definitionCN: 小数；千分之一写作小数点后三位

entries.definition: Extremely small; a description of size with no measure attached.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的（只描述大小，不带刻度）

entries.definition: One of two equal parts; the most familiar fraction for contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 一半（最常见的分数，用于对照）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the -th pattern and the fractional use in measurement.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自 -th 序数规律，以及在计量中的分数用法。

normal.en: Add -th to thousand, just as fourth and fifth carry their -th.
normal.cn: 在 thousand 后加 -th，正如 fourth 与 fifth 都带着 -th。

normal.en: A thousandth of a second is the number on the sports timer’s last screen.
normal.cn: 千分之一秒就是计时器最后那一屏上的数字。

normal.en: The ordinal marks place, the fraction marks a slice: one word, two jobs.
normal.cn: 序数标记位置，分数标记切片：一个词，两种职责。

normal.en: The thousandth visitor is a milestone; a thousandth of a second is a hair’s breadth.
normal.cn: 第一千位访客是一个里程碑；千分之一秒却细如发丝。

normal.en: For the thousandth time is not a count but a complaint.
normal.cn: for the thousandth time 不是计数，而是抱怨。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler carved into a thousand tiny squares, with the last square lit up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被刻成一千个小格的尺子，最后一格亮着。

abstract.en: The same word can be the summit of a count or an almost invisible sliver.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以是计数的顶点，也可以是一片几乎看不见的细条。

abstract.en: Thousandth is where large numbers teach you how small small can be.
abstract.cn: thousandth 是「大数量」教你「小」能小到什么程度的地方。

examples.en: The race was decided by three thousandths of a second.
examples.cn: 这场比赛以千分之三秒之差分出胜负。

examples.en: This was the thousandth copy printed from the old press.
examples.cn: 这是那台老印刷机印出的第一千份。

examples.en: For the thousandth time, put the tools back in the box.
examples.cn: 我都说了一千遍了，把工具放回箱子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扫芯斯」——扫到第一千根芯丝,只剩那么一丝 → thousandth 千分之一

root: thousand（日耳曼语复合词，原指「大百、千」）+ 序数后缀 -th，与 fourth、fifth 构词相同；既表序列中的第一千个，也表一千等分之一，后者在现代计量中尤为常用。

sensesIntro.en: Thousandth has one exact position, one tiny fraction, and one exasperated exaggeration to cover.
sensesIntro.cn: thousandth 要覆盖一个精确位置、一个极小分数，以及一个烦躁的夸张说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler cut into a thousand small squares, with the last one lit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把被刻成一千小格的尺子，最后一格亮着。

branches.en: The position: the last step of the first thousand.
branches.cn: 位置线：第一个千的最后一步。

branches.en: The slice: one of a thousand equal parts.
branches.cn: 切片线：一千等份中的一份。

branches.en: The complaint: a count worn out by repetition.
branches.cn: 抱怨线：被重复磨掉分量的计数。

branches.en: Precision work, where a thousandth of a unit is a real difference.
branches.cn: 精密工作线：单位的千分之一是真实的差别。

branches.en: Exact order and exhausted exaggeration share the same form.
branches.cn: 精确的顺序与疲惫的夸张共用同一形式。

intro.en: Thousandth is a clean -th ordinal; related forms come from the base numeral.
intro.cn: thousandth 是标准的 -th 序数词，相关形式都从基数词派生。

latinIntro.en: Both the base and the suffix are native English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属英语本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.exampleCN: 它把 thousand 变成 thousandth。
